gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the 6,000 W units (Nature's Generator L6000, Anker SOLIX F3800 Plus) deliver their full rating only through the L14-30R at 120/240 V and 25 A, with every 120 V outlet capped at 3,000 W (TT-30R) or 2,400 W (5-20R), so a 5,000 W load must be a 240 V load and takes 20.8 A of the 25 A available.
standout_why: Compared against solarwaypoint.com and holdbackup.com (cited), thiswatt.com, powerbencher.com and thewattguide.com (not cited), and the Anker F3800 Plus page (cited). Solarwaypoint and thiswatt give no outlet or leg figures. Holdbackup names outlet types and a 7,200 W total but no per-outlet watts. Powerbencher says 5,000 W at 120 V is about 42 A and no household outlet can deliver it, but gives no figures for a qualifying unit's outlets. Thewattguide already has the principle ('anything above that must leave the unit through 240V outlets or several outlets at once') and per-120 V figures for Jackery (two 3,600 W banks) and OUPES (3,600 W from 120 V). ChatGPT's own answer also warns that one 120 V socket may not supply 5,000 W. What none has: the Nature's Generator L6000 at all, the 25 A L14-30R limit on the two 6,000 W units, the headroom left once a 5,000 W load is running, or the 1,800 W pass-through cap on a 120 V cord.
decides: It confirms rather than changes the pick. Every unit in the line makes 5,000 W only at 240 V through the L14-30R (or a transfer switch fed from it); none does it from a 120 V outlet. The L6000 qualifies on its maker's manual, but with the tightest margin: a 5,000 W 240 V load leaves 1,000 W in total (about 500 W per leg). The 7,200 W units (Pecron F5000LFP by its maker's '3600W*2' figure) leave 2,200 W, so a shopper running a 5,000 W load plus anything else should take a 7,200 W unit. Pecron's ships early January, which is more than four weeks out. The L6000 passes through only 1,800 W on its 120 V cord; 6,000 W pass-through needs the $119.99 240 V cable and a 14-50R outlet.

findings.label: 240 V outlet rating (manual, section 2.2.1 item 12)
findings.value: "Line 1 and 2 NEMA L14-30R Outlet: Provides up to 120/240Vac 25A 6000W output."
findings.note: The only outlet that carries the full 6,000 W. Troubleshooting 3.6a repeats '240V 25A 6000W maximum'. Arithmetic: 5,000 W ÷ 240 V = 20.8 A of 25 A, leaving 1,000 W (about 500 W per leg).

findings.label: 120 V outlet ratings (manual, section 2.2.1 items 15, 17, 18)
findings.value: TT-30R on Line 2: "up to 120Vac 25A 3000W AC output"; NEMA 5-20R on Line 1 and Line 2: "Each outlet can provide up to 120Vac 20A 2400W output."
findings.note: Largest 120 V outlet is 3,000 W. A 5,000 W load at 120 V would need 41.7 A (5,000 ÷ 120). The manual states no separate per-leg limit; 3,000 W per leg is 25 A × 120 V from its own figures.

findings.label: Pass-through (power relay) limit while plugged into the wall (manual, section 2.5)
findings.value: "can support up to 1800W of power" on the included 120 V cord; "can be increased to 6000W by being recharged by the super charge cable"; switchover "within 10ms"
findings.note: Manual also says 'The L2 outlets are in line with the power input' on the 120 V cord, and an overload breaker trips above 15 A in relay mode. As a plugged-in UPS on a 120 V cord it passes through 1,800 W, not 5,000 W.

findings.label: Cable needed for 6,000 W pass-through
findings.value: Lithium 6ft Super Charging Cable, $119.99; requires a 240 V NEMA 14-50R outlet; "Supports up to 6000W (120/240V) for L6000"
findings.source_title: Nature's Generator Lithium 6ft Super Charging Cable
findings.note: Read through storecheck.py search on naturesgenerator.com; listed as available.

findings.note: The help-center page (https://naturesgenerator.com/pages/help-center/lithium-6000) lists '12 Months' in its spec table and also shows an 'Up to 5-year warranty' badge; the two disagree.

findings.label: Why 5,000 W cannot come from a 120 V outlet on these units
findings.value: 5,000 W ÷ 120 V = 41.7 A; 5,000 W ÷ 240 V = 20.8 A. The largest 120 V outlet read on any unit here is 25 A / 3,000 W (TT-30R on the L6000 and F3800 Plus).
findings.note: Arithmetic on the makers' outlet ratings. Powerbencher makes the general 42 A point for household outlets; no page read applies it to a qualifying unit's own outlets.
